content: The enzyme aspartate aminotransferase, cytoplasmic, is encoded by the GOT1 gene in humans. This enzyme, also known as glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase, is dependent on pyridoxal phosphate for its activity. It exists in two forms: a cytoplasmic form (GOT1) and a mitochondrial form (GOT2). Aspartate aminotransferase plays a critical role in amino acid metabolism, as well as in the urea cycle and the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle. Both forms of the enzyme are homodimeric in structure and exhibit a high degree of similarity in their molecular composition.
